angles: Gartner's enterprise framework: How the 'magic quadrant' lens applies to AI coding agents — Codex, Copilot, Cursor, and Claude Code evaluated on completeness of vision vs ability to execute in enterprise settings

The two-speed enterprise AI coding market: GitHub Copilot dominates large enterprises (56% in 10K+ companies) while Claude Code and Cursor lead startups — driven by procurement, compliance, and risk tolerance differences
Multi-tool is the new normal: 70% of engineers use 2-4 AI coding tools simultaneously — enterprise platform strategy must accommodate heterogeneous tool ecosystems rather than single-vendor lock-in
The productivity paradox: High adoption (90%) coexists with low trust (29%) and measured slowdowns (METR: experienced devs 19% slower on complex tasks) — enterprise governance is the missing layer

Model routing as enterprise strategy: No single frontier model dominates all workflows — routing across Opus (architecture), Codex (terminal), and Gemini (cost) cuts enterprise costs 40-60% while maximizing capability coverage

Gartner's 2028 prediction as catalyst: With 75% enterprise adoption mandated by 2028, organizations need structured evaluation frameworks now — evaluating on security, compliance, code quality, and governance, not just developer preference

Enterprise cost modeling: True TCO for a 10-developer enterprise team ranges from $8,400 (bare subscriptions) to $192,666/year including training, debugging overhead, code review time, and overage charges

The security and compliance angle: AI-generated code has 2.74x the vulnerability rate of human-written code; 63% of devs spend more time debugging AI output — enterprise adoption requires automated guardrails and review workflows
